blogs.title: When “Receipt” Becomes Digital: The Fifth Circuit’s Take on Modern Cancellation Procedures
blogs.description: This post dissects the court’s interpretation of the term “receipt” under Louisiana’s insurance‑premium finance cancellation statute, emphasizing how the Fifth Circuit embraced electronic transmission and automated web‑service calls as satisfying a traditionally paper‑centric requirement. It will explore the implications for insurers, finance companies, and litigants, and consider whether this signals a broader judicial willingness to modernize statutory concepts in the digital age.

blogs.title: The Signature Question: Does Louisiana Law Require a Hand‑Signed Certification for Policy Cancellations?
blogs.description: An analysis of the Fifth Circuit’s determination that a signature is not required on the premium‑finance company’s certification statement. The blog will trace prior Louisiana appellate opinions, the statutory language, and the court’s reasoning, then assess how this decision may affect future disputes over formalities, the evidentiary weight of electronic certifications, and the potential for legislative amendment.

blogs.title: Private Carrier Meets Email: Creative Statutory Construction or Overreach?
blogs.description: A critical look at the district court’s—upheld by the Fifth Circuit—characterization of APAC’s email as a “private carrier” for purposes of the cancellation statute. The article will evaluate the doctrinal basis for this categorization, compare it to traditional carrier jurisprudence, and discuss whether such inventive definitions risk destabilizing statutory interpretation or open the door to flexible, industry‑friendly readings.

blogs.title: Certification of Complex State Law Questions: Why the Fifth Circuit Declined to Send This Issue to the Louisiana Supreme Court
blogs.description: This piece examines the court’s refusal to certify the ambiguous terms of La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550(G)(3) despite the plaintiffs’ push for guidance. It will explore the jurisprudential standards governing certification, the appellate court’s deference to state courts, and the strategic considerations for litigants seeking Supreme Court clarification in niche insurance‑finance disputes.
